# ReadingTime

Estimated reading time, calculated from the word count.

```tsx
import { ReadingTime } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- Beside the date and author of an article, so readers can decide whether to start now.

## When not to

- For video or audio: it measures words.
- As a promise: it is an estimate.

## Examples

### From the text

Pass the text, or the word count if you already have it. The result is rounded up and never less than one minute.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-6">
  <ReadingTime text="Un texto muy corto." />
  <ReadingTime words={1450} />
</div>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  | The text to measure (plain string). Or pass `words`. |
| `words` | `number` |  | Word count, if you already have it. |
| `wordsPerMinute` | `number` | `200` | Reading speed in words per minute. 200 is a careful pace for literary text in Spanish. |
| …rest | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **Machine-readable:** the text is inside a `<time datetime="PT5M">`.
- **Localised:** the phrase comes from `KafkaProvider` labels.
- **Icon** is decorative.
- Rounds up, never below one minute; 200 words per minute by default (a careful pace for literary Spanish).

## Content

- Compute it once at build time with `countWords` if the text is long.
